hook: For forty-five years, the world champion lost roughly one game every six years. In checkers.
story: His name was Marion Tinsley. He won nine world championship matches and never lost one; his opponents gave up playing him for the win and settled for draws. He quit for twelve years out of boredom. So in 1990 they sat him across from a computer called Chinook, a machine searching twenty moves ahead. On the tenth move of the tenth game, it liked its position. Tinsley looked up and said, "You're going to regret that."
number: He wasn't guessing. His notes show he'd seen the end of the game at move eleven. For the machine to know it had already lost, it would have needed to search sixty moves into the future. Seven losses in forty-five years, by most counts.
closer: The computer took his title in 1994, without winning a single game of the match.
full_text: For forty-five years, the world champion lost roughly one game every six years. In checkers. His name was Marion Tinsley. He won nine world championship matches and never lost one; his opponents gave up playing him for the win and settled for draws. He quit for twelve years out of boredom. So in 1990 they sat him across from a computer called Chinook, a machine searching twenty moves ahead. On the tenth move of the tenth game, it liked its position. Tinsley looked up and said, "You're going to regret that." He wasn't guessing. His notes show he'd seen the end of the game at move eleven. For the machine to know it had already lost, it would have needed to search sixty moves into the future. Seven losses in forty-five years, by most counts. The computer took his title in 1994, without winning a single game of the match.
